items.stem: Leishmania, which causes kala-azar, divides by binary fission:
items.answer: in a definite plane, lengthwise
items.markingKey: (b) in a definite plane, lengthwise.

items.stem: Which of these organisms reproduces by regeneration?
items.answer: Planaria
items.markingKey: (c) Planaria reproduces by regeneration. The others: Hydra – budding; some sea worms – fragmentation; Spirogyra – fragmentation.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Amoeba is immortal in the sense that the parent never dies of old age.
Reason (R): The parent Amoeba divides into two daughter cells and disappears into them.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Group these organisms by mode of reproduction, binary fission or regeneration: Leishmania, Planaria, Amoeba.
items.answer: Binary fission: Amoeba, Leishmania. Regeneration: Planaria.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): Binary fission: Amoeba, Leishmania. Regeneration: Planaria.

items.stem: A bacterium divides by binary fission every 30 minutes. Starting with 1 bacterium, how many will be present after 5 hours if none die?
Which of these organisms does NOT reproduce by binary fission?
items.answer: encysted Amoeba under unfavourable conditions
items.markingKey: (d) Encysted Amoeba under unfavourable conditions reproduces by multiple fission, not binary fission. Each of the others (Amoeba, bacteria, Leishmania) reproduces by binary fission.

items.stem: Explain why a seed from a cross-pollinated plant may produce a plant slightly different from both parents.
items.answer: Cross-pollination brings together gametes from two plants with different DNA; fertilisation combines them, producing new combinations (variation).
items.markingKey: 1 mark two parents. 1 mark fusion. 1 mark variation.

items.stem: A bacterium divides by binary fission every 20 minutes. Starting with 2 bacteria, how many will be present after 2 hours if none die?
A bacterium divides by binary fission every 20 minutes. Starting with 10 bacteria, how many will be present after 3 hours if none die?

items.answer: DNA copying
items.markingKey: (d) DNA copying is the making of copies of DNA, which carries the information for inheritance, before a cell divides.

items.stem: Why is reproduction essential for a species even though it is not needed for an individual to survive?
items.answer: Individuals die, and reproduction keeps the population and species going over generations.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: individual survives without it. 1 mark: continuity of species.

items.stem: Define a spore.
items.answer: A tiny reproductive body covered by a thick wall, which grows into a new organism in favourable conditions
items.markingKey: 1 mark: A spore – a tiny reproductive body covered by a thick wall, which grows into a new organism in favourable conditions.

items.stem: Which of the following plants is commonly propagated by grafting?
items.answer: guava
items.markingKey: (a) Guava is propagated by grafting. The others: dahlia – propagated by roots; jasmine – propagated by layering; onion (bulb) – propagated by underground stems.

items.stem: Why are bananas and roses grown by vegetative propagation and not from seeds?
items.answer: They have lost the capacity to produce viable seeds, and vegetative propagation gives plants identical to the parent.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: no viable seeds. 1 mark: identical plants.

items.stem: Sort these plants into those propagated by grafting and those propagated by layering: bougainvillea, guava, jasmine.
items.answer: Propagated by grafting: guava. Propagated by layering: bougainvillea, jasmine.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): Propagated by grafting: guava. Propagated by layering: bougainvillea, jasmine.

items.stem: Sort these plants into those propagated by grafting and those propagated by leaves: Bryophyllum, begonia, guava.
items.answer: Propagated by grafting: guava. Propagated by leaves: Bryophyllum, begonia.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): Propagated by grafting: guava. Propagated by leaves: Bryophyllum, begonia.

items.stem:
Read: Ravi cut a Planaria into three pieces in the lab; each grew into a complete worm in two weeks. He also saw small outgrowths on a Hydra which detached and became new Hydras, and a slice of bread kept in a humid box developed black dots on white threads.
(i) Name the process seen in Planaria. (ii) Name the process seen in Hydra. (iii) Name the organism on the bread and its mode of reproduction. (iv) Are the offspring in these cases similar to or different from the parent? Why?
items.answer: (i) Regeneration. (ii) Budding. (iii) Rhizopus (bread mould); spore formation from sporangia. (iv) Similar, because only one parent is involved and there is no fusion of gametes.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.stem: If all members of a crop are produced by vegetative propagation from one plant, what risk does the farmer face? Explain.
items.answer: They are genetically identical, so a disease or pest that attacks one can wipe out the whole crop; there is no variation to resist it.
items.markingKey: 1 mark identical. 1 mark disease risk. 1 mark no variation.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "Joining a cut stem of one plant (scion) onto a rooted plant (stock) so they grow as one."
items.answer: grafting
items.markingKey: (c) Grafting is joining a cut stem of one plant (scion) onto a rooted plant (stock) so they grow as one.

items.stem: A gardener in Pune wants many mango trees giving fruit of exactly the same quality as her best tree, and quickly. Should she sow seeds or use grafting? Give two reasons.
items.answer: Grafting: the scion from the best tree keeps exactly its fruit quality, while seeds give variation; grafted trees fruit earlier.
items.markingKey: 1 mark choice. 1 mark each reason.

items.stem:

items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

items.stem: Define the pistil (carpel).
items.answer: The female reproductive part of a flower, made of stigma, style and ovary
items.markingKey: 1 mark: The pistil (carpel) – the female reproductive part of a flower, made of stigma, style and ovary.

items.stem: Which of these is a unisexual flower?
items.answer: cucumber flower

items.stem: Why do the petals and sepals of most flowers wither after fertilisation?
items.answer: Their job of attracting pollinators and protecting the bud is over; the plant's food goes to the developing fruit and seeds.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: job over. 1 mark: resources to fruit.

items.stem: Classify these as a part of the stamen or a part of the pistil: ovule, ovary, anther, stigma.

items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): A part of the stamen: anther. A part of the pistil: ovary, ovule, stigma.

items.stem:
Read: A flower of a mustard plant has four sepals, four yellow petals, six stamens and a pistil. Bees visit it, and later the petals fall and a long pod develops containing many seeds.
(i) Is the flower unisexual or bisexual? (ii) What is the role of the bees? (iii) Which part of the flower develops into the pod? (iv) What did the ovules develop into?
items.answer: (i) Bisexual. (ii) They carry pollen to the stigma (pollination). (iii) The ovary. (iv) Seeds.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.stem: Arrange these steps of sexual reproduction in a flowering plant in the correct order: (1) the male gamete reaches the ovule; (2) the zygote develops into an embryo; (3) the male gamete fuses with the egg to form a zygote; (4) the ovule becomes a seed and the ovary a fruit.
items.markingKey: Correct sequence: the male gamete reaches the ovule → the male gamete fuses with the egg to form a zygote → the zygote develops into an embryo → the ovule becomes a seed and the ovary a fruit.

items.stem: A papaya grower finds that one of her plants never bears fruit although it flowers every year. Suggest a reason and a remedy.
items.answer: Papaya bears unisexual flowers on separate plants; the plant is probably a male plant. She should grow female plants with a few male plants nearby for pollination.
items.markingKey: 1 mark male plant. 1 mark unisexual. 1 mark remedy.

items.stem:

items.stem: Compare sexual reproduction in humans and in frogs in terms of fertilisation, development and care of the young.
items.answer: Humans: internal fertilisation in the oviduct; the embryo grows in the uterus fed through the placenta; viviparous; long parental care. Frogs: external fertilisation in water; many eggs laid; egg → tadpole → adult by metamorphosis; oviparous; little parental care.

items.stem: Om studies a frog spawn of 1000 eggs in a village pond near Nashik. If only 5% of the eggs survive to become adult frogs, how many frogs develop? Why does the frog need to lay so many eggs?

items.markingKey: 5% of 1000 = 50. External fertilisation and no parental protection mean heavy losses.
